overview.body:
**Bhaiṣajyaguru** ​(*bhaisajyaguru*) — ‌Healing, ‌Medicine, ​Lapis-Lazuli Light ​· ​Medicine master ​— ​belongs ‌to the ​Buddhist ​tradition, where ‌it ​is catalogued ‌under ​the ‌domain "Healing, ​Medicine, ​Lapis-Lazuli Light". ​The ​name ​means "Medicine ‌master"[^1].

​**Bhaiṣajyaguru** belongs ‌to ​the ‌Buddhist tradition, ​where ‌it is ​associated ‌with ​healing, medicine, ​lapis-lazuli ‌light.[^2]

PuniCodex ‌restores ‌the name ​as ​**Bhaiṣajyaguru** ‌and serves ​its ​temple at ‌[bhaisajyaguru.com](https://punicodex.com/bhaisajyaguru/). ​The ​restoration preserves ‌at ​least one ‌distinctive ​feature ​— a ​diacritic ​or a ‌distinctive ‌letter ​— that ‌the ​ASCII form ​loses, ‌and exactly ‌one ‌historically ‌valid Unicode ​restoration ‌exists, which ​places ​the ​name in ‌Tier ​1. The ​plain ​ASCII ‌form *bhaisajyaguru* ​survives ​as a ​modern ‌convenience ​imposed by ‌the ​early domain-name ‌system; ​the restoration, ‌not ‌the ​fallback, is ​the ​form the ​project ‌defends ‌as philologically ​complete[^2].

the-name.body:
The name ​is attested ‌in Devanagari ‌as **भैषज्यगुरु**. Etymologically ​it means ​"Medicine master"[^1].

​Sanskrit Bhaiṣajyaguru, ​from bhaiṣajya 'healing, ​remedy' + ‌guru 'teacher'; ​the Medicine Buddha ​of lapis-lazuli ‌radiance.

The ​ASCII form *bhaisajyaguru* ‌survives only ​because the ‌early domain-name system ​could not ​carry diacritics; ​it is ​a technological compromise, ​not an ‌ancient spelling. ​The Unicode restoration ‌**Bhaiṣajyaguru** recovers ​the full ‌diacritic detail of ​the scholarly ‌transliteration directly ​in the address ‌bar. The ​restoration preserves ​at least ‌one distinctive feature ‌— a ‌diacritic or ​a distinctive letter ​— that ‌the ASCII ​form loses, and ​exactly one ‌historically valid ​Unicode restoration exists, ​which places ‌the name ​in Tier ‌1.

The letter-by-letter ​transformation runs:

​- **b** ​→ **B** — ​Same, capitalized
‌- **h** ‌→ **h** — ​Same
- ‌**a** → ​**a** — Same
​- **i** ‌→ **i** ‌— Same
‌- **s** → ‌**ṣ** — ​Ṣ: retroflex ‌sibilant, underdot (IAST ​ṣ)
- ​**a** → ​**a** — Same
‌- **j** ​→ **j** ​— Same
- ​**y** → ‌**y** — ​Same
- ​**a** → **a** ​— Same
‌- **g** ​→ **g** — ‌Same
- ​**u** → ‌**u** — Same
​- **r** ‌→ **r** ‌— Same
- ​**u** → ​**u** — ​Same

The ​canonical temple for ‌this name ‌is served ​at **bhaisajyaguru.com**[^2].

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation ‌of ​the ​name is ​**/bhaisajyaguru/** ​— ​Buddhist ‌Reconstruction.[^1]

​Phoneme ​by ‌phoneme:

​- ‌**B** ​— Initial ‌character ​of ​the ​restored ​form ​Bhaiṣajyaguru.
‌- ​**haiṣajyaguru** ‌— Remainder ​of ‌the ​name, ‌preserving ​the ‌distinctive ​marks ​of ‌the ‌Buddhist tradition.

‌For ​the ​modern ‌speaker, ​the ​closest ‌approximation ​is: ​'BHAISAJYAGURU' ‌— pronounce ​the ‌restored ​form ​with ​attention ​to ‌the ‌preserved ​diacritics ‌and length.

​Kindred ​and ‌historical ‌forms ‌of ‌the ​name:

‌- ​**Buddhist** ​— Bhaiṣajyaguru, ​the ‌restored ​Unicode ​form ​of ‌the ​name

​Bhaiṣajyaguru ​is Tier ‌1 ​because ‌the ​Buddhist ‌form ​preserves ‌distinctive ‌features ​that ​ASCII loses: ​stress, ​length, ‌or ‌special ​characters.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌**Bhaiṣajyaguru** ‌circulate ​within the ​Buddhist ​corpus, where ​the ​figure ‌embodies healing, ​medicine, ​lapis-lazuli ‌light.[^1]

### ​Primary ‌Attestation (Sources)

​Bhaiṣajyaguru ‌is ​attested in ​the ​canonical Buddhist ​sources ​as ‌a figure ​associated ‌with ​healing, medicine, ‌lapis-lazuli ​light.[^1]

### ‌Name ​and ‌Meaning (Etymology)

​The ​name means ‌"Medicine ‌master" ‌and reflects ​the ​figure's ‌role in ​the ​tradition. **Bhaiṣajyaguru**, ‌the ​Medicine ​Buddha, presides ‌over ​the pure ‌land ​of ​Vaiḍūryanirbhāsa. He ​vowed ​to heal ‌the ‌physical ​and mental ‌afflictions ​of ​beings and ‌is ‌invoked in ‌healing ‌rituals ​across Mahāyāna ‌and ​Vajrayāna Buddhism.[^1] ​His ​deep-blue ‌color and ​medicine-bowl ​emblem ​identify him ‌in ​iconography. The ​twelve ​great ‌vows of ​Bhaiṣajyaguru ‌include the ​promise ‌to ​cure disease, ‌relieve ‌poverty, ​and guide ​beings ​toward awakening ​through ‌medical ‌and spiritual ​means.[^1]
